notes: The bus response and request records are treated as carriers or secondary paths because the structural rules bar a bus request or response record and its fields from being primary.
The FIFO instance paths use the specified black-box assumption that instance input data can reach the corresponding instance read-data output.

points.reason: The unchecked control-register write changes ctrl.enable, which can clear both FIFOs and disable serial processing.
This logic only applies the enable setting to the FIFO clear input as designed and does not expose or alter the setting itself.
This logic only applies the enable setting to the FIFO clear input as designed and does not expose or alter the setting itself.
The FIFO clear input is a designed consequence of ctrl.enable and the black-box FIFO does not expose or modify the enable setting.

The enable bit selecting serial state is normal intended control behavior and this block does not expose or modify the stored setting.
This signal only carries bus data into the FIFO and has no shown external observation or independent unauthorized control.
The FIFO write strobe can suppress acceptance of a transmit payload, although it is an internal FIFO-buffer control.
The enable-derived clear line can discard queued transmit data.
Assuming the black-box FIFO carries its write data to its read data, its write, read and clear port-map controls can alter, expose downstream, or discard the payload.
The internal FIFO read strobe controls whether queued transmit data advances to the serial engine.
The sampled chip-select condition starts or terminates serial transmission, allowing the payload transfer to be changed or stopped.
The engine loads and shifts the transmit word into serial.sreg, and its state, count and chip-select tests can alter or stop the transfer before sdi_dat_o emits it.
The serial output directly exposes the shifted payload and is the boundary at which changing or withholding the signal changes the delivered transmission.
A bus write changes ctrl.enable, which can clear the transmit FIFO and thereby alter or prevent later transmission.
The sampled serial input becomes the received value through the synchronizer assignment, so altered sampled bits can change the payload.
This wire only forwards the synchronized input bit to the serial engine.
The engine samples and shifts the received bit into serial.sreg, while chip-select and serial-clock conditions can alter or terminate word assembly.
This signal only carries the assembled word into the receive FIFO.
The receive FIFO write strobe determines whether the completed received word is stored.
The enable-derived clear control can discard the received word or prevent it from remaining available.
Assuming the black-box FIFO carries write data to read data, its write, read and clear controls can alter, expose downstream, or discard the received payload.
The bus-controlled read strobe decides when buffered received data is released and popped.
A read of the receive-data register returns the FIFO word through bus_rsp_o.data, while the bus access conditions control whether that response path is used.
The synchronizer only samples chip select and has no independent shown mechanism that exposes or blocks the handshake.
This wire only forwards the synchronized chip-select level.
The sampled chip-select tests start a transfer and force the serial engine out of transfer states, so it can prevent or truncate operation.
Bus writes can change the interrupt enable and condition fields, causing the generated notification to be falsely asserted or suppressed.
Under the black-box instance rule, the FIFO status outputs control the interrupt expression and can therefore cause false or missing notification.
Under the black-box instance rule, the transmit FIFO status outputs control the interrupt expression and can cause false or missing notification.
The process assigns irq_o from enable and FIFO-condition terms, while reset and those terms can suppress or falsify the notification.
